what_its_for: Atenolol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and chest pain (angina). It is also used after a heart attack to help protect your heart. It works by slowing your heart rate and reducing the workload on your heart, which helps lower your blood pressure and reduce chest pain.
how_to_take: Take atenolol by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do NOT stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping it abruptly can cause serious heart problems. If you need to stop, your doctor will slowly lower your dose over time.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. Common starting doses are 25 mg to 50 mg once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose up to 100 mg per day if needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store atenolol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking atenolol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and make side effects like dizziness worse. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to prevent dizziness or fainting. Do not take cold medicines, decongestants, diet pills, or stimulants without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as they can raise your blood pressure. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a very slow heart rate (less than 60 beats per minute), severe dizziness or fainting, shortness of breath or trouble breathing, swelling in your legs or feet, chest pain that is new or getting worse, sudden weight gain, cold or numb hands and feet, feeling very tired or weak, signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your blood pressure readings are consistently too high or too low.
when_it_works: Atenolol starts working to lower your blood pressure within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit. Even if you feel fine and have no symptoms, keep taking it every day as directed — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, but it can still cause serious harm if left untreated.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of atenolol, especially dizziness and a slow heart rate. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney problems: Atenolol is removed from the body through the kidneys. If your kidneys do not work well, your dose may need to be lowered. Tell your doctor about any kidney problems. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Atenolol may harm an unborn baby and can pass into breast milk. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: The safety and effectiveness of atenolol in children have not been fully established. Use in children should only be under a doctor's close supervision. Diabetes: Atenolol can hide some warning signs of low blood sugar (like a fast heartbeat). Check your blood sugar more closely and tell your doctor if you have diabetes. Asthma or breathing problems: Atenolol can cause breathing difficulties in people with asthma, COPD, or other lung conditions. Make sure your doctor knows about any breathing problems before you start this medicine.
